name: verifiable integrity
headline: Integrity you can *verify*
sub: Share a branch, and the receiver's machine proves every byte. Identical content collapses to one copy across the whole network.
say: Reason two: integrity you can verify instead of trust. When someone shares a branch of their hive, you receive signatures, and your machine verifies that every byte matches. Identical content collapses into one copy no matter how many people reference it, and the network becomes a global cache — if anyone near you already holds a resource, the signature finds it. Sharing a hash is sharing a proof.
